provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Original mechanism: each row holds at most two coloured cells; if their colours form the unordered pair {4,7} or {1,8}, the right (higher-column) cell slides toward the left cell until adjacent, leaving background behind. The factory pushes the original +column direction vector through the D4 transform (row reversal for d4>=4, then clockwise rotation (dr,dc)->(dc,-dr) per quarter turn). If the resulting vector is horizontal, lines are visible rows, otherwise visible columns; if it points toward increasing index, the anchor is the lower-index cell and the mover slides toward lower index, otherwise the anchor is the higher-index cell and the mover slides toward higher index. Colour roles are specialized as constants: background = palette[0], partner pairs = {palette[4],palette[7]} and {palette[1],palette[8]}. The emitted program scans each visible line directly, walks consecutive non-background cells starting from the anchor side, and moves the far partner to the cell adjacent to the anchor.
draft_notes.limitations: Background is fixed to palette[0] (the constructor always uses 0 as background; a most-common-colour heuristic could tie on narrow grids, so the constant is safer). Lines with more than two coloured cells never occur in the constructor domain; for such inputs the program follows the archived solver's consecutive-pair scan from the anchor side. Demonstrations are not consulted; the partner table is the fixed lookup from the generator. Fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule.
